messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English between two adult friends with noticeably different personalities. One is more careful and practical; the other is more impulsive and sarcastic. Let their personalities come through naturally in dialogue, word choice, pacing, and small actions. Do not label or explain their personalities to the reader. Keep both characters believable and avoid caricatures, clichés, and melodrama.

“We should probably leave.”

Alex looked at the clock. “We've been here eleven minutes.”

“Exactly.”

Jordan smiled. “You always say that like eleven minutes is some kind of emergency.”

“It is when you said you'd only be gone for five.”

“I said approximately five.”

“You said five.”

“I implied five.”

Alex folded her arms. “That's not how time works.”

Jordan picked up the receipt from the table and turned it over. “You know, for somebody who claims to be spontaneous, you really enjoy schedules.”

“I enjoy knowing where I'm supposed to be.”

“Same thing.”

“No, it isn't.”

Jordan grinned. “See? This is why I keep you around.”

“You don't keep me around. I tolerate you.”

“Whatever helps you sleep.”

Alex stood and grabbed her bag. “Are you coming?”

Jordan stayed seated.

“Jordan.”

“One second.”

“You said that three minutes ago.”

“I've had a lot to think about.”

“About what?”

Jordan looked at the receipt in her hand. “Whether you were serious about leaving.”

Alex stared at her.

Jordan finally stood. “Okay, okay. I'm coming.”

“You're impossible.”

“And yet you've waited for me.”

Alex opened the door and held it for her. “Don't make me regret it.”

Jordan stepped through with a grin. “Already did.”

Alex shook her head, but she was smiling as she followed.”
